input.prompt:
You review a set of behaviour specifications that will each be implemented, one after the other, on the same domain classes. Find specifications that cannot all be true together.

## Product intent
- Product type: game
- Audience: players who want to play a single-player minesweeper puzzle
- Goal: Let players clear a minefield by revealing safe cells and flagging mines, with a clear win or loss outcome.
- Scope: A playable minesweeper game consisting of a grid board, mine placement, cell reveal and flag interaction, and win/loss detection with a game timer and mine counter.
- The model must cover: Board grid and cell states (hidden, revealed, flagged); Mine layout and adjacency counts; Game session state (in progress, won, lost) and elapsed time; Difficulty settings (grid size and mine count)
- Do NOT model: User accounts and login; Online leaderboards or cross-player multiplayer; Payments or monetization; Server-side back-office administration

## Specifications
- SPEC-001 [Adjacency count] (Game): Given a game with mines placed and a safe cell at a position When the mine layout is fixed Then the cell's adjacent_mine_count equals the number of mines in its up to eight neighbouring cells.
- SPEC-002 [Zero expansion] (Game): Given a hidden cell with adjacent_mine_count 0 in an in-progress game When the player reveals it Then all its neighbouring hidden cells are revealed and any neighbour with count 0 continues the expansion recursively.
- SPEC-003 [Zero expansion stops at numbered cells] (Game): Given a zero-count reveal that reaches a neighbour with count greater than 0 or a flagged neighbour When expansion runs Then that neighbour is revealed only if hidden and not flagged, and expansion does not continue beyond it.
- SPEC-004 [First-click safety] (Game): Given a game in ready status When the first cell is revealed Then mines are placed so that the revealed cell and all its neighbours have has_mine false, and the layout is fixed.
- SPEC-005 [Flag placement on hidden cells] (Game): Given an in-progress game and a hidden cell When the player flags it Then the cell state becomes flagged and flag_count increases by one; Given a revealed cell When the player flags it Then the board is unchanged.
- SPEC-006 [Flag removal] (Game): Given a flagged cell in an in-progress game When the player removes the flag Then the cell returns to hidden and flag_count decreases by one; Given a flagged cell When the player attempts to reveal it Then the cell remains flagged and is not revealed.
- SPEC-007 [Right-click cycle] (Game): Given a hidden cell When the player right-clicks it Then it becomes flagged; Given a flagged cell When the player right-clicks it Then it becomes hidden; Given a revealed cell When right-clicked Then it is unchanged.
- SPEC-008 [Mine counter may go negative] (Game): Given a game with mine_count M and flag_count F When the counter is displayed Then it shows M minus F, including negative values when F exceeds M.
- SPEC-009 [Loss on mine reveal] (Game): Given an in-progress game When the player reveals a mine Then status becomes lost, ended_at is set, all mine cells are shown as revealed, and flagged cells without mines are marked as wrong.
- SPEC-010 [Win on all safe cells revealed] (Game): Given an in-progress game When the last non-mine cell is revealed Then status becomes won, ended_at is set, and every unrevealed mine cell becomes flagged.
- SPEC-011 [Terminal state rejects changes] (Game): Given a game in won or lost status When the player reveals or flags any cell Then the board and status are unchanged; When the player restarts Then a new game is created.
- SPEC-012 [Timer starts on first reveal] (Game): Given a game in ready status When the first cell is revealed Then started_at is set and elapsed time begins; Given a game in ready status When a flag is placed Then the timer does not start.
- SPEC-013 [Timer stops at session end] (Game): Given an in-progress game When the session is won or lost Then elapsed_seconds is fixed at the value at that moment and no longer increases.
- SPEC-014 [Timer display cap] (Game): Given elapsed time greater than 999 seconds When the timer is displayed Then it shows 999.
- SPEC-015 [Invalid operations ignored] (Game): Given any game state When the player reveals a revealed cell, acts after game end, or targets a position outside the board Then the board and session state are unchanged.
- SPEC-016 [Restart resets session] (Game): Given a game in any status When the player starts a new game at a chosen difficulty Then a new board is created with status ready, elapsed time zero, and no mine layout fixed.
- SPEC-017 [Difficulty grid and mine count] (DifficultySetting): Given a player starting a game When Beginner is chosen Then the board is 9x9 with 10 mines; Intermediate yields 16x16 with 40 mines; Expert yields 30x16 with 99 mines.
- SPEC-018 [Board edge boundaries] (Game): Given a cell on the board edge or corner When adjacency is computed Then only neighbours inside the board are counted, giving fewer than eight neighbours.
- SPEC-019 [Grid cell presentation] (Game): Given a revealed cell with count 1 When the board is rendered Then the tile is flat light grey and the number is blue.
- SPEC-020 [Flag and header presentation] (Game): Given a flagged cell When rendered Then a red flag is shown; Given a game in progress When the header is rendered Then mine counter, timer and restart button are visible above the grid.

Report only real contradictions: two or more specifications that demand incompatible results for the same situation (for example one says an inquiry is accepted when a field is missing and another says it is rejected). Do not report overlaps, duplicates, missing detail or style differences.

Respond STRICTLY with JSON, no commentary:
{"conflicts": [{"specs": ["<spec_id>", "<spec_id>"], "reason": "<one sentence naming the incompatible demands>"}]}
Use an empty list when there are none.
